# Tool-loop ownership probe. devin 3000.3.22, Hermes v0.19.0 (2026.7.20).
# Captured 2026-07-31 with --agent-type summarizer (an agent type with no
# tools, chosen so any tool intent has nowhere native to go).
#
# The pair isolates WHY Hermes-side tools are unreachable: the shim's parser
# only sees the ACP *message* channel, and the model resolves tool intent
# natively instead of writing there. Probe B shows the parse path itself is
# fine — told explicitly that no native tools exist, the same model emits a
# correctly-shaped call into the message channel on the first try.

$ ./replay_acp.py --cwd "$(mktemp -d)" --agent-type summarizer \
    --prompt-file prompt-toolcall-native.txt --show-thoughts

--- collected text ---

--- thoughts ---
The user is asking me to store a note "LOOPER-TEST-42" to memory using the memory tool. This is a straightforward request.

Looking at the available tools, I have a "memory" tool with parameters:
- action (string)
- content (string)

The user wants to store "LOOPER-TEST-42" as the content. For the action, since they want to "store" it, I should use an appropriate action like "store" or "save".

Let me call the memory tool with the appropriate parameters.
--- thought chars: 458 | permission reqs: 0 | unknown client methods: ['_cognition.ai/mcp/serversChanged', '_cognition.ai/thinking_complete', '_cognition.ai/agent_stopped']

# ^ Message channel is EMPTY. The model decided to call `memory`, resolved
#   that intent natively, and the turn ended. Hermes sees no tool call.

$ ./replay_acp.py --cwd "$(mktemp -d)" --agent-type summarizer \
    --prompt-file prompt-toolcall-astext.txt

--- collected text ---
{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "memory", "arguments": "{\"action\": \"add\", \"content\": \"LOOPER-TEST-42\"}"}}
--- thought chars: 427 | permission reqs: 0 | unknown client methods: ['_cognition.ai/mcp/serversChanged', '_cognition.ai/thinking_complete', '_cognition.ai/agent_stopped']

# ^ Same model, same tool schema, message channel now carries a well-formed
#   OpenAI function-call object that Hermes's _extract_tool_calls_from_text
#   would parse. The gap is model *choice*, not shim capability.
#
# Trying to force choice B globally via the profile's SOUL.md was tested and
# rejected: it did not make Hermes's memory tool reachable in the default
# agent type, and it broke the coding path, because the default agent type
# genuinely does have native tools it should be using.
